events.title: The execution of Girolamo Savonarola
events.shortBlurb: The Dominican preacher who had ruled Florence with calls to repentance was hanged and burned in its great square…
body: On 23 May 1498 the Dominican Girolamo Savonarola was hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria at Florence, together with his friars Domenico da Pescia and Silvestro Maruffi; their ashes were thrown into the Arno. He was forty-five years old.

Born at Ferrara in 1452, he entered the Dominicans at Bologna and in 1491 became prior of San Marco in Florence, where his preaching of repentance and his prophecies of chastisement drew the city. After the expulsion of the Medici in 1494 he stood at the head of the republic, and at the carnival of 1497 his followers burned profane books and finery in the 'bonfire of the vanities.'

His denunciation of corruption in high places reached Pope Alexander VI, who excommunicated him in May 1497; when his party fell, he was arrested, tortured into a confession he later retracted, and condemned by ecclesiastical and civil tribunals alike. Never canonized, he has remained a disputed figure — false prophet to some, herald of reform to others.
